title: Corrupted BIOS black screen recovery via USB Flashback
step: Insert drive into designated BIOS Flashback USB port
claim: Locate the specific rear I/O USB port bordered by a white or grey outline labeled 'BIOS Flashback' or 'Q-Flash Plus'. Insert the USB flash drive. CRIT
verdict: BIOS flash USB must be formatted as FAT32. Missing this specification could lead to failed flash.
correction: Always specify: USB drive must be formatted FAT32, 4GB or larger

title: ATX 24-Pin Power Sequence and PS_ON Green Wire Triage
step: Measure DC rail voltages with multimeter
claim: 12V DC, red wires for +5V DC, orange wires for +3.3V
verdict: 12V value of 3.3V outside normal ATX ±10% range (10.8V-13.2V). Verify context.

title: Solid state drive is over 90% full
claim: Press Start, type 'Defragment and Optimize Drives', select your SSD, and click 'Optimize' to run TRIM and reclaim stale flash blocks.
verdict: Defragmenting an SSD is unnecessary and increases write wear. Windows Optimize already uses TRIM on SSDs.
correction: Never run disk defragmentation on SSDs. Use TRIM via Windows Optimize instead.

title: Overheating, loud fans, and thermal throttling
step: Repaste CPU and GPU with high-grade thermal paste
verdict: 0% IPA is too low for electronics cleaning. Leaves water residue that causes corrosion.
correction: Use 90%+ IPA for electronics. 99% IPA is optimal.

title: Motherboard pushing excessive voltage (ASUS MCE / Gigabyte Enhanced)
verdict: 10°C seems unusually cold for normal operating temp claim - verify context
